title: Distinct cochlear cell types associated with genetic susceptibility to sensory and metabolic hearing loss in older adults.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: abstract only; Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500 (also on a direct fullTextXML fetch); supplementary files not retrievable; no GEO/SRA/Zenodo/Dryad links found; text-mined accessions are only four OMIM-style numbers (603681, 601071, 620521, 602666), which point to genes, not datasets.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study design comes from the abstract: it combines existing human GWAS (genome-wide association study) results for sensory and metabolic age-related hearing loss with existing mouse cochlear single-cell RNA-seq, using scDRS (single-cell disease relevance score, a statistical scoring tool). No new data table or row count was seen.

a1_downloadable.note: No data deposit found; the paper reuses others' GWAS and mouse single-cell data. Human hearing-loss GWAS inputs are likely from cohorts such as UK Biobank or similar, which need access applications for individual data; not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no prediction target in a table. Any label (e.g., a gene's hearing-loss association, or a cell's disease score) would have to be constructed by joining GWAS gene scores to single-cell expression.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs exist only as references to other studies' data; not checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown; the natural unit (cochlear cell types or GWAS loci) is small — tens of cell types, a handful of risk genes.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Mouse cochlear single-cell sets are typically modest, but not checked.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts available to compare; full text inaccessible.

a8_label_provenance.note: The paper's main outputs, scDRS cell scores, are statistical model outputs computed from the very expression features a model would use — circular as an ML label.

backbone.name: Geneformer or scGPT (single-cell foundation models) would be the only plausible fit

integration.partner_dataset: GWAS Catalog hearing-loss loci; public mouse cochlear scRNA-seq in GEO
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which cochlear cell types carry the genetic risk for each hearing-loss subtype — already the paper's own question, answered by statistics rather than ML.

controls.positive_control: Known deafness genes enriched in hair cells (named in the abstract as the sensory-component result).
controls.negative_control: Random matched gene sets, which scDRS already uses.

honest_claim_h3: A model could at most re-rank cochlear cell types by enrichment of hearing-loss GWAS genes, which the paper already does with a dedicated statistical tool.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use cochlear single-cell gene activity to predict which cell types carry inherited risk for each kind of age-related hearing loss.
plain_idea.train_on: Mouse inner-ear single cells (gene expression profiles) paired with human hearing-loss association scores per gene; number of examples unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Per-cell or per-gene risk score; the 'truth' is itself a statistical score computed from association-study results, not a direct measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Hearing-loss geneticists could prioritise cell types for therapy, but the paper already answers this with a standard statistical method, so ML adds little.

ml_idea: None viable: this is a GWAS-to-single-cell enrichment analysis with no deposited table or measured label; any ML target would be constructed from the features.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A before any data was located.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find a data availability statement listing a new deposited table with a measured per-item outcome; none was found.

verdict_reason: Secondary analysis paper (GWAS + reused mouse single-cell data via scDRS) with no new deposited data; no label column exists (A2), the obvious label is a statistical score derived from the features (A8), and full text and supplement were not retrievable.
